dataset.name: Neurophysiological Dataset of Stress Resilience During Human-Computer Interaction
excluded_files_and_content: EEG, fNIRS, eye-tracking, MATB-II and other task data
demographicCDrisk.csv, resilience scales, and all task/stress/resilience annotations
dataset.license: Open Data Commons Open Database License v1.0; cite PhysioNet dataset and respect attribution/share-alike obligations
dataset.candidate_assessment: Metadata-only local search found no reference to this dataset in project configs, manifests, decision documents, or dataset catalog. This does not prove prior-use lineage outside the searched project. No target signal values have been read.

purpose: Frozen-weight, signal-only transfer of WESAD-trained SSL rejection scores to an independent E4 collection using deterministic injected faults; no stress, task, resilience, clinical, or performance prediction.

frozen_models.ssl: All nine WESAD-only compact native PhysioME-inspired v7 fold/seed checkpoints; both fixed scores: physiome_raw_1nn and physiome_restoration
frozen_models.comparator: The nine previously selected WESAD-only derivative_roughness_hybrid fold/seed artifacts
frozen_models.normalization_and_thresholds: Use only the matching frozen WESAD training moments, WESAD calibration ranks at alpha 0.05, and existing frozen assignment rules; do not refit or retune. Verify checkpoint hashes against the frozen v7 manifests before any target inference.

signal_preprocessing.source_scope: Download and inventory only the PhysioNet PPG/E4 folder. Read only the four allowed E4 signal files. No broad archive extraction. Preserve the publisher archive and member hashes.
signal_preprocessing.windowing: Use every complete, non-overlapping 10-second segment on the four-channel common time intersection. Start at the first common timestamp. Do not inspect task/event markers or select by signal/model outcome. Do not interpolate across timestamp gaps.
signal_preprocessing.rate_rule: Read published per-file metadata and sample timestamps. Accept native 32/64/4/4 Hz; otherwise use deterministic anti-aliased rational resample_poly conversion to those model rates only if timestamps establish the actual rate, with Kaiser beta 5 and denominator limit 10000. Stop before scoring if timestamps/rates are absent, ambiguous, inconsistent, or outside validated conversions.
signal_preprocessing.unit_rule: Use file metadata/PhysioNet README to establish units. Convert only documented E4 accelerometer units to the frozen WESAD raw-count convention (64 counts/g). Keep BVP, EDA and TEMP in documented native units. Stop before scoring if any conversion would rely on signal-value heuristics or undocumented assumptions.
signal_preprocessing.alignment_and_eligibility: Use per-sample timestamps and their intersection. Require finite values, strictly increasing timestamps, at least 100 eligible windows per included participant, and no gap >1.5 times the within-file median interval. Report every excluded participant/recording and reason. Require at least 10 eligible participants; otherwise stop before scoring.
signal_preprocessing.normalization: Use each frozen model's own WESAD training-fold channel moments; estimate no cohort statistics.

analysis.inference_unit: participant; first average recordings and frozen fold/seed models within participant
analysis.faults: Apply the unchanged structured_faults_v3 operators: drift, source-relative range clipping, sample hold, and mean-imputed gap, each at low/medium/high severity. Single-modality targets are primary; pair targets, no-ops, clean windows, and per-family breakdowns are secondary/descriptive.
analysis.fault_seed: Use the frozen structured_faults_v3 deterministic source/window/family/modality SHA256 seed rule, with participant token and zero-based common-window index. No labels or outcomes affect fault generation.
analysis.primary_endpoint: Participant-equal mean standardized fault-excess MSE among retained sampled nonzero-dose single-fault windows, with equal modality weighting and fixed WESAD scales, at each frozen WESAD threshold.
analysis.coverage_guard: For each SSL score, the participant-bootstrap one-sided 95% lower confidence bound for paired coverage difference versus hybrid must be greater than -0.05.
analysis.zero_coverage_rule: If any included participant has zero retained windows in any required modality for an SSL score, that score's primary selective-risk contrast is non-estimable and fails the joint rule. Do not impute risk or remove the participant.
analysis.inference: Participant-paired bootstrap with 10000 resamples and seed 20261017; percentile 95% intervals. Paired sign-flip test with 100000 flips and seed 20261018 for two primary risk contrasts; Holm correction. No window-level inference.
analysis.success_rule: At least one frozen SSL score must yield an estimable lower selective risk than the simple hybrid with Holm-adjusted two-sided p < 0.05 and pass the five-percentage-point coverage guard. Otherwise the independent confirmation fails; do not select a score or threshold post hoc.
limitations: Designed perturbations are not natural unusability, sensor failure, or task harm
A positive result would confirm only frozen synthetic-fault transfer in this cohort
No task, stress, resilience, clinical, glucose, or performance claim
Participant sample size, protocol context, and eligibility are reported; windows are not independent replicates
No protocol change after target signal values or model outcomes are inspected

preflight_stop_gates: Before signal values are parsed or model scores computed, verify this exact protocol's public deposit, dataset version, allowed-file inventory, archive integrity, model hashes, and release license.
Read only ACC/BVP/EDA/TEMP; do not open task markers, stress labels, questionnaires, demographics, HR/IBI, EEG/fNIRS, MATB-II or eye-tracking files.
Verify actual units, time formats, rates, synchronization, coverage, participant count and deterministic unit/rate conversion using signals only. Stop before scoring on any unresolved ambiguity.
No threshold refitting, model selection, cohort normalization, target training, or post-outcome protocol amendment.
